summary: The page says scripts/release.py stamps, commits and tags a release; the script now says it never commits or tags (CI does, ADR 0021). Its runtime dependency list also leaves out httpx, tenacity, tomlkit, questionary and markdown-it-py.

The page puts round caps in checks/, but they live in verdicts/rules.py and commands/common.py. It also says the plugin payload holds no code and lists only skills/, agents/, hooks/ and min-cli-version, but the payload ships the generated opencode/loop-harness.js, which ST-05 allows by name.

Four claims are false: the verb groups leave out ask, judgements and delegate (and schema at the top level); state-guard is wired to Edit|MultiEdit|Write|NotebookEdit|Bash, not Edit|Write|Bash; init writes six gitignore lines including .loop/exports/, not five; and the ticket stage comment leaves out fixing.

The diagram has the operator 'signs, or delegates per ticket'. Per-ticket eval delegation is gone: a standing grant (ADR 0029) can cover the whole repository, an epic or named tickets, and eval delegate was removed.
Every stage and edge in the diagram, including the five done-outside edges and the two reconcile edges, matches the transition table, and the eight stages match the Stage type.
The ten versioned data objects, the 38 event kinds plus the retired delegation in KINDS, the TicketState fields, atomic writes and the rule files it names all match the code.
The CI jobs and their order, the release.yml dry run and version pull request, and the release-tag.yml checks, build, tag and SHA256SUMS release all match the workflows and scripts.

The flow ends with 'done. Next: loopctl ticket next' after ticket done, but next_step names loopctl ticket land SLUG until the closing commit is on the integration branch, and implement-ticket lands the work as its own step. The landing step is missing.
The routing matches manifesto section 1, and the blocks it names (plan-invalidated, finding open two rounds) are block codes the code has; plan-invalidated can be set by hand.

The page says the state guard and commit gate match the Bash command string; checks/shell.py now parses Bash as commands, not text (RC-08), as command-surface also says. The state-guard box also names only Edit, Write and Bash, while the hook covers MultiEdit and NotebookEdit too.
